- **Authority.** The runtime of slice 1 hosts no domain operation: it answers
  handshake, status and stop. It confers no authority, signature or presence, and a
  client that attaches gains nothing it did not have standalone.
- **Slicing.** B35 is delivered in three specs, each reviewed on its own:
  `pose-optional-worktree-runtime` (identity, endpoint, handshake, lifecycle,
  standalone fallback: R1-R4), `pose-worktree-runtime-resident-cache` (R5, R7: the
  resident reuse of the B33 views, reconciliation, typed results) and
  `pose-worktree-runtime-qos-and-measurement` (R6, R8: budgets, short queries
  protected from heavy checks, measured thresholds). Budgets and thresholds are
  fixed from a measured synthetic corpus with a declared environment, never from a
  historical sample.

## Amendment: what the optional worktree runtime delivered, and where it departs (B35, 2026-11-10)

The three slices are done and each was reviewed independently: `pose-optional-worktree-runtime`
(identity, protected endpoint, handshake, lifecycle, standalone fallback),
`pose-worktree-runtime-resident-cache` (hosted read checks, typed results, resident memo) and
`pose-worktree-runtime-qos-and-measurement` (admission lanes and the measurement), with two engine
specs that the measurements called for (`pose-index-input-binding-reads-each-transfer-once`,
`pose-governance-audit-skips-pure-git-reads`). The statement above that "the runtime of slice 1
hosts no domain operation" was true of slice 1 only. What stands now, and what differs from the
decisions of this ADR:

- **Hosted operations.** The runtime hosts five read checks (`review-check`, `closeout-check`,
  `artifact-check`, `surface-check`, `roadmap-check`) through `pose runtime run`, as the user that
  started it, in its worktree; a hosted request carries the caller's identity and is refused,
  before any handler runs, when it does not match the runtime's engine, build, protocol, schema
  or worktree; the caller's environment digest must equal the runtime's. They are not writes, but
  they may refresh derived files as they do standalone (published atomically); a command that may
  have run (deadline, lost reply) is never repeated elsewhere unasked, which is how the decision
  "an ambiguous committed write requires a receipt before a retry" is met for these commands.
  Hosted commands go through the domain's own entry (`mainCommand`), not a new typed interface:
  the typed-domain extraction of the first bullet of the decision stays with B31.
- **Caches.** The B33 views are not what the runtime reuses (the measurements showed they do not
  address the cost). It keeps, between commands, the output of the Git reads that are pure
  functions of object ids or of the commit HEAD named when they ran, keyed by the commit, the
  content of the shallow file and of the repository config, with a byte budget and
  least-recently-used eviction; no watcher exists, so "watch events are hints" is met by not
  using them: freshness comes from the key, and nothing about mtime or a clean tree is taken as
  proof. The scoped Git batch reader is untouched.
- **Budgets and QoS.** Admission is by two lanes (`short`, `heavy`) with slots and bounded queues
  and a bound on the memo; the global concurrency bound is the sum of the slots. **Not delivered:**
  CPU quota or affinity awareness, and per-command memory or I/O limits; the runtime bounds what
  it admits and keeps, not what each command consumes. The measurement records latency, the
  runtime's resident set and CPU time per scenario, including two simultaneous heavy checks, on one
  environment; it is not a general benchmark.
- **Platforms.** Unix domain socket on Linux and macOS (credentials of the peer from the
  operating system); Windows runs every command standalone and `pose runtime status` says so.
  The named pipe is a follow-up.
- **Status.** The decision stands as amended for the delivered scope; what is not delivered above
  is not adopted and needs its own spec before it is claimed.

The implementer's notes say this profile allows the plan tools, but it doesn't. Rule (g) requires the required tools (`validate` ×2, `roadmap-check`, `assess-integrate`) to be run and passed. I won't claim they passed when I didn't run them, so they are marked `deferred` with the reason. Re-run the review with those commands allowed if you want an attestation that can be recorded.

## What I checked by reading

- **Specs:** all six member specs and both engine specs (`pose-index-input-binding-reads-each-transfer-once`, `pose-governance-audit-skips-pure-git-reads`) are `status: done`.
- **Draft specs:** the three the roadmap promises are `status: draft` (`pose-runtime-resource-limits-per-command`, `pose-runtime-windows-named-pipe`, `pose-checks-route-to-the-runtime-by-default`).
- **Measurement report:** the fourth run's T1–T7 match what the ADR's 2026-11-10 amendment claims, and its stated limits (one environment, no CPU quota) are disclosed.
- **Runtime security:** the runtime directory is mode 0700 and owner-checked, and the socket is 0600 and owner-checked. Peer credentials are checked before any byte is read (`worktreeruntime/runtime.go:406`). Every hosted request is compared field by field against the runtime's identity (`runtime.go:453`), and the environment digest must match (`runtime_host.go:93`). An outcome that may already have run is never retried (`runtime_host.go:212`, `256`).

## Findings

- **F1 (medium): the resident Git memo can return stale output.** At `pose-mcp/internal/pose/resident_git_memo.go:79`, the key covers only `.git/config` and `shallow`. It leaves out global, user and system Git config and `[include]`d files. `RawHistoryGit` (`spec_trailers.go:46`) doesn't neutralise those, so a change to `~/.gitconfig` (for example `log.follow`) while the runtime runs leaves a cached read different from what standalone would give.
  - This contradicts the code comment ("cannot differ", `resident_git_memo.go:19`) and the ADR amendment (`ADR:294`).
  - It weakens the B35 exit gate's deterministic output and B33's "no stale cache".
  - The gap is tracked only in the draft spec `pose-runtime-memo-hits-and-git-config-key`. The roadmap's "Estado" paragraph (`roadmap:11-14`) doesn't list it among what isn't delivered.
- **F2 (low): `memo_hits` is miscounted.** At `pose-mcp/internal/cli/runtime_host.go:134/145`, it is the difference of a global counter, so with concurrent lanes it includes other commands' hits.
- **F3 (low): the ADR's status line is out of date.** It still reads "Proposed … No IPC … daemon lifecycle … is implemented/adopted" (`.pose/adr/2026-10-14-shared-domain-and-optional-worktree-runtime.md:5`), which contradicts the delivered state described in the 2026-11-10 amendment.
- **F4 (low): one promised limit has no requirement.** The roadmap (`roadmap:12`) puts CPU quota and affinity in a draft spec. `pose-runtime-resource-limits-per-command` R1 (line 36) requires only CPU and memory limits per lane: no affinity, and I/O appears in the goal but in no requirement.
